idiom_name: message struct with json tags plus ToMessage/FromMessage functions in one adapter package
implementation_notes: Go has no reflection-based mapping culture, so the idiom is explicit conversion: the message is a dedicated struct carrying `json:"..."` tags, the mapper is func ToMessage(o domain.Order) OrderMessage alongside func FromMessage(m OrderMessage) (domain.Order, error), and both live in the adapter package nearest the consumer so the domain package never imports an encoding package. encoding/json (or a schema-first codec when the contract is IDL-owned) performs the wire half; the classic mapper object collapses into those functions plus slice helpers. MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON are the exception, justified only when the message needs a shape its struct cannot express.
pitfalls: Embedding the domain struct in the message struct publishes every exported field and re-couples the shapes - embed only when the wire shape really is the domain shape.
encoding/json ignores unknown keys and leaves absent fields at their zero value: a producer adding a required field looks fine until the consumer notices a zero, so validate after unmarshalling.
A nil slice or map in the domain becomes null on the wire unless the mapper normalises it; consumers in other languages are usually stricter than Go.
time.Time marshals as RFC 3339 with nanoseconds - if the contract wants unix seconds or a date, the mapper must convert explicitly.
